claims.text: Ti40Ni40Al10V5Cr5 can exist as a single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloy before aging.
The Al, V, and Cr additions in Ti40Ni40Al10V5Cr5 stabilize its single-phase solid-solution state.
Solution treatment at approximately 1050 °C for 2–4 hours under argon will chemically homogenize the proposed alloy.
Aging at approximately 650 °C for about 6 hours after solutionizing will induce NiTi-type precipitates in the proposed alloy.
The induced NiTi-type precipitates will have a B2 crystal structure.
The aging treatment will produce a uniform dispersion of nanoscale, coherent precipitates.
Nanoscale ordered precipitates impede dislocation motion and thereby strengthen the matrix.
The proposed precipitates will inhibit grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
B2 precipitates will provide slip-frustration hardening in the proposed Ti–Ni-dominant alloy.
B2 precipitates will provide Orowan strengthening at elevated temperature in the proposed alloy.
The aged alloy will have higher yield strength than the as-solutionized alloy.
The aged alloy will have better creep resistance than the as-solutionized alloy.
The aged alloy will have improved overall mechanical stability during high-temperature or extreme-environment testing.
The as-cast or solely solutionized baseline lacks beneficial nanoscale precipitate strengthening.
The proposed strengthening effect is applicable across mechanical tests conducted from 600 °C to 900 °C.
Poorly controlled aging may produce coarse or inhomogeneous precipitates that reduce the desired mechanical enhancement.
A controlled comparison of aged and as-solutionized samples using tensile, creep, hardness, microscopy, and fractography measurements can test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain statistically significant gains in both yield strength and creep resistance, or failure to obtain the intended precipitate morphology, is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires precipitation of a distinct B2 phase, which makes the aged microstructure multiphase, while the boundary says processing conditions remain in the single-phase region.

The baseline is described as either as-cast or solely solutionized, but the predicted comparison and experimental control specifically use the as-solutionized condition; as-cast and solutionized states are not interchangeable controls.
